newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Man dies in Australian ammunition blast.
newsitem.headline: Man dies in Australian ammunition blast.

text.p: A massive explosion at an Australian ammunition factory, described by an eyewitness as like "an atomic bomb", killed one person on Tuesday and shook towns up to 50 kms (30 miles) away.
The explosion at the Australian Defence Industries factory at Mulwala in southern New South Wales state occurred around 8.30 a.m. (2130 GMT), police said.
The cause of the blast was not yet known.
"I just saw the mushroom cloud, it was like an atomic bomb, and the siren and I knew it was a disaster," Mulwala resident Clive McCawley told Australian Broadcasting Corporation radio.
An ambulance official told Reuters an unidentified man was killed in the blast. "If anyone was in the area (of the blast) they would be very lucky to be alive," the spokeswoman said.
She said five people were treated for shock but there were no other casualties except for the dead man.
The Mulwala ammunitions factory on the New South Wales-Victoria state border is the country's largest ammunitions factory and has produced ammunition since World War Two.
Australian Defence Industries could not say what caused the blast, pending an investigation.
McCawley, who lives across the road from the factory, said the explosion occured at a bunker storage, surrounded by dirt mounds in case of an explosion.

"If it didn't have the mounds there I think the whole of Mulwala would have gone up," he said. "The explosion just went up." Police at Corowa, 50 kms (30 miles) to the east, said they also felt the blast.
